sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and rule wording
sections.what: Holds the rule code, the message shown to the developer, and the patterns that match transfer-style names and rights tables.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the rule text and patterns in one place so they are easy to update. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The message points to a legal document by section, so renaming that document breaks the reference.

sections.name: check_source
sections.title: Ownership transfer checker
sections.what: Reads a Python file and returns a violation for each function with a transfer-style name and each owner-changing call on a rights table.
sections.why: Likely reason: catches ownership changes at the code level before they ship. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Matching uses names only, so code that changes ownership under a different name will not be caught.

summary: Flags code that would directly transfer or rewrite land ownership, so that ownership changes are only recorded as evidence.
purpose: Enforces a legal rule that the software must not change land ownership on its own.
why: The message names a legal reference and says ownership changes must go through a competent authority. The reason for the rule is taken from the message text.
how: Parses a Python source file and looks at every function name for transfer-style words. It also looks at calls such as set or update owner made on something that looks like a rights table, and records each match as a violation.
inputs: Python source text and the file path it came from.
outputs: A list of violation reports, each with the rule code and a message pointing to the legal document.
risks: Source that is not valid Python raises an error. Name matching is by pattern, so unusual names may slip past or harmless names may be flagged.
debug: If a violation seems wrong, check the name patterns at the top. If the check crashes, check the source for syntax errors.
